headline: Good morning, Frankie. The blackout is over, and the answer turns out to be the calmest possible one: nothing ran wild. The FA-ADS watchdog woke back up at 3:38 AM your time and reported all clear — and it solved the three-day mystery. The "$300 Plan" was not spending unwatched through two nights; it was paused. You paused it yourself, in Power Editor, Wednesday at 12:41 PM PT. That is why spend has been $0 and leads flat at 21 ever since — not a broken funnel, a deliberate stop. Lifetime spend is $205.39, sixty-eight percent of the plan, every kill gate green, and the R4 $240 notify line the AM brief feared had "probably already been crossed" was in fact never crossed, because spend stopped four days ago. So the panic in this morning's edition was wrong, and it is worth saying plainly. What is actually on the table now is smaller and clearer. The watchdog is asking one question back: was that pause meant to stay off? That is your call, and only yours — resume it, or leave it parked, but say which, because right now the machine does not know. Two things the pause does not fix, and this quiet is the cheapest time there will be to fix them: cost per booked call still cannot be measured at all — the digest says "4 booked," the watchdog says "no CRM source connected," and until one CRM is wired, nobody can say whether this campaign works; and compliance is still 0/7 on day eight — b7 (your CA license #) and b3 (the TX registration) are the two named reasons the last account was banned, and a paused campaign with no new leads landing is the safest moment there will ever be to place them. One more thing worth noticing: you are not actually dark. You paused a campaign in Meta on Wednesday — you are in the tools, just not in the mailbox. So the ask is three lines from you today: resume or leave off; the NPN + CA license # (or the one-line state rule); and who owns the resume decision. Everything Chitraksh needs to wire the CRM and pin the watchdog is already queued behind those.
